content.text:
I think your instinct is right for **general automated config editing**, but this particular update is narrow enough to work.

Pkl can derive values through inheritance, expressions, and imports. After evaluation, you know the resulting value, but that doesn’t necessarily tell you which source expression to edit. A syntax-preserving parser helps retain formatting; it doesn’t resolve that ambiguity. That’s a real cost of using a programmable configuration language. [Pkl language reference](https://pkl-lang.org/main/current/language-reference/index.html)

The Renovate proposal avoids most of that: it finds **literal package URLs and replaces their versions**. It doesn’t need to evaluate or rewrite the surrounding configuration. I’d support that approach, subject to reviewing the implementation—particularly how its line-based matching handles block comments and multiline strings. The reported test coverage alone doesn’t establish that. [Renovate discussion](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/45740)

Where I’d push back on the hk discussion is the implication that **an older Pkl package necessarily means something is wrong**. The executable and schema/builtins are separate dependencies. Version drift is worth making manageable, but the survey doesn’t demonstrate incompatibility or establish that every executable update requires a schema update. Updating builtins can also change lint behavior, so keeping those changes explicit has value. [hk discussion](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1344)

My take:

- Welcome the upstream Renovate manager for literal dependency updates.
- Don’t require everyone to pin hk instead of choosing `latest`.
- Treat broader commands like “add a step” or “change this setting” as a separate Pkl editing problem.

**Pkl makes general editing difficult; updating explicit package pins is a tractable exception.** I wouldn’t reject this contribution on editability grounds, but it doesn’t remove that architectural concern.
i think it's fine but yes, hk is generally backwards compatible with older configs

Right—that makes this a useful convenience, with no need to frame version drift as broken configuration. An older Pkl pin can be intentional while the hk executable stays current.

I’d welcome the Renovate manager and clarify in the hk discussion that keeping both versions synchronized is optional because hk is generally backward compatible with older configs.
post a reply to the hk discussion
I’ll post that to the hk discussion, welcoming the manager and clarifying that version synchronization is optional.
